title: The Telehealth Correction: Economic Implications of Expiring Waivers
summary: As pandemic-era reimbursement parity waivers expire, the healthcare market faces a sharp correction in virtual care supply. This analysis quantifies the revenue risk for rural providers and the shifting cost burden to patients.

children.text: The rapid expansion of telehealth during the public health emergency was underpinned by temporary reimbursement parity. As these waivers sunset, we are witnessing a significant market correction. Providers who capitalized on virtual visits as a primary revenue stream must now pivot to hybrid models or face solvency risks.

CMS has signaled a return to pre-pandemic fee schedules for remote monitoring codes. For rural health clinics (RHCs), this effectively cuts the margin on virtual visits by 40%. The economic implication is a forced consolidation of independent practices into larger health systems that can absorb the administrative overhead of complex billing requirements.
Without parity, telehealth becomes a loss leader—a service patients demand but providers cannot afford to supply.
